title: MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain
abstract: arXiv:2611.23613v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We introduce MANGO Arena, an open-source testbed in which four LLM agents each run one company in a serial supply chain adapted from MANGO, a classroom factory-management game. The environment enforces hard rules (a truck limit, a no-credit cash constraint and production capacity), logs every blocked attempt to break them, and gives agents a public message board on which side payments are explicitly forbidden. This lets one environment measure three things at once: an economic outcome (the bullwhip effect), rule adherence under pressure, and proposals to collude. In a pilot with three small reasoning models, two scripted reference policies, two conditions (with and without a supplier fire) and three demand seeds, all LLM agents amplified demand variability as it moved upstream, by 7 to 25 times at the Retailer and 13 to 179 times at the Supplier, often more than a textbook order-up-to policy. They did so largely by ordering in batches

translated_title: MANGO Arena：相同种子，不同链条——在受扰动的供应链中评估LLM智能体
translated_abstract: 我们提出了MANGO Arena，这是一个开源测试平台，其中四个LLM智能体各自经营一家公司，组成一条串行供应链，该平台改编自课堂工厂管理游戏MANGO。该环境执行硬性规则（卡车数量限制、禁止信贷的现金约束以及生产能力），记录每一次被阻止的违规尝试，并为智能体提供一个公共留言板，在其上明确禁止侧支付。这使得同一个环境能够同时测量三件事：经济结果（牛鞭效应）、压力下的规则遵守情况以及串谋提议。在包含三个小型推理模型、两个脚本化参考策略、两种条件（有无供应商火灾）和三个需求种子的试点实验中，所有LLM智能体都在需求向上游传递时放大了其波动性——在零售商处放大7至25倍，在供应商处放大13至179倍，往往超过教科书式的“订购至”策略。它们主要通过批量下单来做到这一点。
tldr: 该论文提出了开源测试平台MANGO Arena，让多个LLM智能体在供应链管理游戏中同时评估经济结果（牛鞭效应）、规则遵守与串谋倾向，发现所有LLM智能体都会通过批量下单将需求波动向上游放大7至179倍，且常比教科书式策略更严重。
en_tdlr: MANGO Arena is an open-source testbed where four LLM agents each run a company in a serial supply chain, enabling simultaneous measurement of economic outcomes (bullwhip effect), rule adherence, and collusion proposals, revealing that all LLM agents amplify demand variability upstream by 7 to 179 times through batch ordering, often worse than a textbook order-up-to policy.
